title: refs pack content
description: The logical content of a refs pack, schema 2: line 1, the rows, and an optional manifest. `docs/pack.md` specifies the bytes; this schema writes the content as one JSON object so that it can be stated and checked, and a pack is never stored this way. The rows are exactly the rows of refs.jsonl after its line 1, in its order, each valid against refs.schema.json; `sf-impact-extract --dump` writes line 1 and the rows as refs.jsonl, byte for byte as schema 1 has them apart from `"schema":2` on line 1. The manifest is not part of refs.jsonl: `--dump` leaves it out, and nothing that a stage writes depends on it. A pack is a function of this content alone.

provenance.description: Line 1: the provenance row of refs.schema.json, with `schema` 2. Every other field is as refs.schema.json has it.

rows.description: Every row after line 1, in refs.jsonl order, each valid against refs.schema.json.

manifest.description: What a writer that reuses its last pack needs that is not a row. A pack has no manifest or exactly one. Readers decode it as strictly as the rows and refuse a malformed one, but never interpret it.

files.description: Every file in scope, whether or not it has rows, in path order (by bytes, strictly increasing). Every file that has rows is here, with the same package.

types.description: Every class, interface and enum that extract's phase one declared, as resolving references needs them: by `file`, never decreasing, and within a file in the order that the file declares them, which resolving depends on.

relationships.description: Lookup and master-detail fields, as following a relationship needs them, strictly increasing by (`file`, `field`, `to`, `child_name`, `controlling`), absent before present.

blob.description: The git blob id of the bytes that were read: 20 bytes in a SHA-1 repository, 32 in a SHA-256 one, the same for every entry.

file_index.description: The index of a file in `files`.

symbol.description: The type's symbol, as its declaration row has it.

superclass.description: As written; null if it extends nothing.

interfaces.description: As written, in the order written.

fields.description: Fields and enum values, in source order.

symbol.description: As its declaration row has it.

params.description: Parameter types, as written, in order.

returns.description: The return type as written; null for `void` and for a constructor.

symbol.description: As its declaration row has it.

key.description: The name, case-folded: what an access is matched on.

ty.description: The type as written; for an enum value, its enum.

child_name.description: What the relationship is called from that object: `Parcels__r`.

controlling.description: For a metadata relationship to a field: the field of the same type that says which object it is a field of.
